newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft, but off lows after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft, but off lows after FOMC.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker, but retook lost ground on Wednesday after the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee announced it would not alter its discount rate, traders said.
"Trading dried up after the same-day market closed (at 1130 EST) and dealers decided to sit and wait for the FOMC decision," said a trader.
"Some dollars flowed in after the decision, but it came too late in the session to make much differenece," he added.
The FOMC decision was announced 15 minutes before the Mexican foreign exchange market closed.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and the 24-hour contract closed 0.5 and 0.4 of a centavo weaker at 7.9100/7.9150 and 7.9050/7.9090 per dollar, respectively.

Dealers said that dollars could be in supply in the foreign exchange market on Thursday and thus prop up the peso, in response to the FOMC meeting, but they still expected the peso to slide over the coming weeks.
"We may see the peso firm up a little at the open tomorrow with some euphoria carried over from the FOMC meeting today, but dealers will have to cover (dollar) positions later," a trader said.
The same-day peso had meanwhile closed 0.3 of a centavo firmer at 7.9070/7.9120 per dollar.
